To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

diagnostic radiography students are not learning what is expected in terms of professionalism and that the current curriculum is failing to develop the professionalism of diagnostic radiography students.

The research revealed a lack of convergence of professional attitudes and values over time, suggesting that the curriculum and the hidden curriculum did not transform personal frames of reference to meet expected requirements.
the students in our study did not develop a strong professional identity and that the hidden curriculum undermined their professional development.

the development of professionalism in the context of a changing health service.
how students learn and how this learning can be facilitated.
the development of professionalism in diagnostic radiographers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study revealed a need to develop a curriculum which attends to the context of professional practice and the hidden curricula in order to ensure students emerge able to deal effectively with the complexities of radiography practice and espouse a multidimensional professional identity.
diagnostic radiography students do not develop the full range of professional attributes expected of them and that the curriculum does not provide the necessary conditions to facilitate this.
this cohort of radiography students were not learning and developing professionalism in the way that the curriculum was intended.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

this study provided evidence of how the hidden curriculum of practice can undermine professional development and how the values, attitudes and beliefs that underpin practice can be transformed by a more reflective, critical and reflexive approach to learning.
the curriculum was not sufficiently effective in transforming students' attitudes to professionalism and that the clinical environment undermined professional development.
we have shown that the curriculum needs to be revised in order to meet the needs of the profession and to prepare graduates for the challenges of professional practice.

we must ensure that the curriculum we design and deliver is able to support the development and maintenance of professional values and ideals that are relevant and meaningful to students.
we need to be more explicit about what we are teaching and how we are teaching it.
